why this file exists: The corpus declares a stop reason in its own vocabulary, because a verdict reached from a guard that fired before the property was evaluated is not the verdict it looks like, and the reason is the only place that difference is visible. The format publishes no reason codes, so the only way to read a stop reason out of this implementation is to match its prose. That is a defect in the format rather than in the implementation, and this file is where the cost of it is paid: one map per implementation, maintained by whoever runs the corpus, going stale the moment a message is reworded. A reason code in the format would delete this file.
matchedAgainst: the first line of the message the verifier emits, lowercased
